Description:
The NURBS twin of ConesTangentAtMantlePoint: two identical cones touching TANGENTIALLY at one point of
their mantles, then united, intersected and subtracted both ways. Neither mantle is a ConicalSurface -
both cones are solid.ruled between two exact nine pole NURBS circles, so both are RuledSurface and the
contact has to be found by the general search on ISurface rather than by the canal form of a quadric.

coneA is the ruled solid between the circle r = 19 at z = 0 and the circle r = 10 at z = 18. Its mantle
lies on the cone with apex (0, 0, 38) and half angle atan(1/2); the apex itself is cut away, which is
what the ruled construction needs - a NURBS circle of radius zero is not a curve.

coneB is coneA rotated by 180 degrees about the surface NORMAL of coneA at one point of its mantle:
  P = (14.25, 0, 9.5)   a point of the ruling from (19, 0, 0) towards the apex (0, 0, 38), a quarter of
                        the way up, so it is well inside the truncated part
  n = (2, 0, 1)         the outward normal there - perpendicular to the ruling (-19, 0, 38), since
                        -19*2 + 38*1 = 0, and to the circumferential direction (0, 1, 0)

Rotating about the normal at P fixes P and fixes the tangent plane at P, so coneB touches coneA at P and
both are tangent to the same plane there. That is the point of the case. A cone touches its tangent
plane along a whole ruling, so both cones touch that plane along a ruling, and the two rulings are
different lines crossing at P. The intersection curve of the two mantles therefore has a NODE at P - two
branches crossing - which is the degenerate situation a surface/surface intersection has to survive.

The angle is 180 degrees on purpose: the rotation is then an involution, coneB = f(coneA) AND
coneA = f(coneB), so the pair is symmetric and the two differences must come out equal. Under it the
base circle of coneA lands at centre (-1.9, 0, 3.8) and its top circle at (12.5, 0, -7), 18 apart as
they must be, with the axis direction (0.8, 0, -0.6).
Expected:
Both operands are the same truncated cone and coneB is a rigid image of coneA, so every measured
quantity must come out the same for both:
  volume      pi*18/3*(19^2 + 19*10 + 10^2) = 3906*pi = 12271.0609049217
  area        lateral pi*(19+10)*sqrt(18^2+9^2) = pi*29*20.1246117975 plus the two lids pi*361 and
              pi*100, together 3281.7508581065
  edgeLength  the two circles measure as their chord polygons 4*r*sqrt(2) (see
              RuledSolidsFromNurbsCircles), 107.4802307404 and 56.5685424949, plus the two seams
              2*20.1246117975: 204.2979968303
coneA reaches z from 0 to 18 and |x|, |y| <= 19; coneB is its rigid image.

The results are pinned by three exact identities, none of which needs a computed value:
  1  volume(coneUnion) + volume(coneInter) = volume(coneA) + volume(coneB) = 7812*pi = 24542.1218098434
  2  volume(coneAminusB) = 12271.0609049217 - volume(coneInter)
  3  volume(coneAminusB) = volume(coneBminusA), from the involution - the sharpest of the three

The one remaining unknown was computed independently by Monte Carlo over the bounding box of coneA,
8e6 samples, using the exact cone volume as a control variate:
  volume(coneInter)     5182.3 +- 3.7
  volume(coneUnion)     24542.1218098434 - that = 19359.8
  volume(coneAminusB)   12271.0609049217 - that =  7088.8 +- 4.1 (measured directly), same for
                        coneBminusA
So the results are checkable against real values to about a tenth of a percent, not merely captured.

WHAT MAY LEGITIMATELY VARY. How many solids each difference falls into is NOT fixed by this prose. In
ConesTangentAtMantlePoint, where the same construction is carried out on ConicalSurface, each difference
came out as two solids - a main body and a pair of lobes that meet the rest only at the tangency point,
so they are one non manifold solid and the split is right. The truncation here changes how far the
second cone reaches, so the same is likely but not guaranteed; whatever comes out has to be judged
against the volume identities above before its baseline is recorded.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
OK since 2026-09-20, and the second paragraph has to be read before any recorded number of this case is.

WHAT THE BOOLEAN NOW DOES, and it is right. The case was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-09-17, when all four
operations hit the assertion "loops.Count should never be 0" inside BooleanOperation. All four return
now, and at ae347d29 they already did, so the repair predates 284004f1. The SHAPE is the one the
Expected section demands:
  coneInter     one solid, Euler 2, eight faces - four RuledSurface and four planar
  coneUnion     one solid, Euler 2, extent -19,-19,-15 .. 19,19,19, exactly the union of the two
                operand extents
  coneAminusB   TWO solids, the main body and the pair of lobes that meet it only at the tangency point
  coneBminusA   TWO solids, likewise
and the geometry is checked against values the code under test had no part in:
  volume(coneInter)   5183.538    against 5182.3 +- 3.7 by Monte Carlo               0.3 sigma
  volume(coneUnion)   19358.560   against the exact identity union + intersect = coneA + coneB, which
                      forces 24542.1218098434 - 5183.538 = 19358.584                 1.0e-06
Both are read with Solid.Volume through inspect.properties, and calls 15 to 20 pin them - including that
every part of both differences, the lobes among them, stays above 300. So a real regression of the
boolean fails this case loudly even though its recorded fingerprint would not notice.

WHAT THE RECORDED FINGERPRINT USED TO BE, AND WHY IT IS RIGHT NOW. Until 2026-09-21 ShellMetrics
measured these bodies wrongly and by a lot - coneUnion 18928.1196638 against 19358.58 true (-2.2 %) and
coneBminusA#1 202.675680244 against about 333 (-39 %). The giveaway was the second one: coneB is a rigid
image of coneA, so coneAminusB and coneBminusA are congruent, their lobes measured the SAME area and the
SAME edgeLength - and different volumes, which congruent shells cannot have.

The cause was Border.Area on a rational curve: BSpline2D.GetArea fell back on the area of
Approximate(false, 0.0), an arc approximation with no defined accuracy that degenerates into straight
lines for a rational spline. A planar face contributes 1/3*d*A to the volume, with d the distance of its
plane from the origin, so ONE area error produced DIFFERENT volume errors at different positions - which
is exactly how two congruent lobes ended up 130.5 apart. BSpline2D now integrates that area instead
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and this case moved accordingly:
  coneBminusA#1 volume   202.675680244 -> 333.178747282, now 8.5e-05 from its congruent twin
                         coneAminusB#1 at 333.150484119, where it was 39 % away
  coneAminusB#1 area     867.679962462 -> 970.708699597, and coneBminusA#1 the same to 5e-08
  coneUnion volume       18928.1196638 -> 19364.9500935, now 3.3e-04 from the 19358.58 that
                         union + intersect = coneA + coneB forces, where it was -2.2 %
A detail worth keeping, because it is the mechanism in one observation: coneAminusB#1 changed its AREA
but NOT its volume. Its planar face lies in z = 0, where the flux density is zero, so an area error
there never reached the volume in the first place. Position dependence, exactly as described.

The assertions of calls 15 to 20 are unaffected by any of this: they read Solid.Volume, which never went
through Border.Area, and they already held while the fingerprint was wrong. They stay because they are
what makes a real regression of the boolean fail this case loudly.

params.message: the ruled solid between exact circles r = 19 and r = 10 that are 18 apart is a truncated cone, V = pi*h/3*(R^2+R*r+r^2) = 3906*pi = 12271.0609
coneB is a rigid image of coneA and must have the same volume
the intersection of the two tangent cones, 5182.3 +- 3.7 by Monte Carlo
union + intersect = coneA + coneB = 24542.1218, so the union is 24542.1218 - 5183.5 = 19358.6
coneA minus coneB is the main body plus the pair of lobes; every part, the lobes included, is above 300
the involution forces coneB minus coneA to be congruent to coneA minus coneB, so its lobes are above 300 as well
